candidate_reports.remark: A waterspout was reported 5 SE of Big Coppitt Key in Hawk Channel. The Monroe County Emergency Manager observed a mature_ tilted waterspout oceanside of Sugarloaf Key at 750 am EDT. Due to the distance from land_ there was no observed spray ring.

candidate_reports.remark: The Monroe County Emergency Manager observed a mature_ tilted waterspout about 10 miles north of Sugarloaf Key at 750 am EDT. Due to the distance from land_ there was no observed spray ring.

candidate_reports.remark: A waterspout was observed oceanside of Stock Island with a visible funnel. However_ the funnel was tilted approximately 45 degrees with no parent contact with the cloud base_ which then dissipated shortly thereafter.
candidate_reports.ugc_name: Hawk Channel from west end of Seven Mile Bridge to Halfmoon Shoal out to the reef

candidate_reports.remark: A member of the public reported a likely mature waterspout to the north of Cudjoe Key. The report came in through social media with a photo. The visible portion of the condensation funnel extended from the base of the cloud at a 45-degree angle_ and was a moderate amount of thickness. The bottom half of the waterspout was obstructed by the homes and trees near the reporter.
candidate_reports.ugc_name: Gulf of America from West End of Seven Mile Bridge to Halfmoon Shoal out to 5 Fathoms

candidate_reports.remark: Multiple reports of two waterspouts were made from members of the public via social media. The first waterspout was very skinny_ nearly vertical_ and a spray ring was visible when it reached the mature stage. The first waterspout lasted approximately 6 minutes. As the first waterspout reached the mature stage_ a second waterspout developed close by from the same parent cell. The second waterspout initially was nearly vertical and skinny as well_ but tilted to a 45-degree angle and grew thicker as it reached the mature stage. The second waterspout lasted approximately 10 to 12 minutes_ and dissipated before reaching land.
candidate_reports.ugc_name: Hawk Channel from west end of Seven Mile Bridge to Halfmoon Shoal out to the reef

candidate_reports.remark: A member of the public reported seeing twin or sister waterspouts in Marathon_ FL around 712 pm EDT earlier in the evening. The report came in via social media with a picture and Broadcast media forwarded the photo to us by tagging us in the message. The first waterspout on the left showed the visible condensation funnel extended from the base of the cloud to just behind the homes in the picture. The condensation funnel was skinny. A spray ring was not visible due to homes and trees obstructing the view. The second waterspout on the right was slightly larger with the condensation funnel extending about a quarter of the way down from the base of the cloud. A spray ring was also not visible due to homes and trees obstructing the view.
candidate_reports.ugc_name: Bayside and Gulfside from Craig Key to West End of Seven Mile Bridge

candidate_reports.remark: Corrects previous waterspout report from 3 W Marathon. A member of the public reported seeing twin or sister waterspouts in Marathon_ FL around 712 pm EDT earlier in the evening. The report came in via social media with a picture and Broadcast media forwarded the photo to us by tagging us in the message. The first waterspout on the left showed the visible condensation funnel extended from the base of the cloud to just behind the homes in the picture. The condensation funnel was skinny. A little later on_ a video came in on social media of the first waterspout near the Seven-Mile Bridge. The condensation funnel was clearly more moderate sized and clearly had a robust spray ring at the water surface. The second waterspout on the right was slightly larger with the condensation funnel extending about a quarter of the way down from the base of the cloud. A spray ring was also not visible due to homes and trees obstructing the view.
candidate_reports.ugc_name: Bayside and Gulfside from Craig Key to West End of Seven Mile Bridge

Preliminary highly-localized damage to one residence in the Silver Shores community between Tavernier and Rock Harbor investigated by Emergency Manager. Time is approximate. A large enclosed porch was destroyed with a section of porch roof deposited in a tree approximately 500 feet to the west southwest. A landfalling waterspout was observed by the public and the event is being reviewed for refinements in timing and intensity.
